title: Lab 7 — Quiz 2
subtitle: Bacterial Genetics — gene expression, codons, operons

questions.explanation: Transcription (by RNA polymerase) makes an mRNA transcript from DNA; translation (by the ribosome) makes protein from mRNA.

why.D: Information doesn't flow from protein back to mRNA.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme is responsible for transcription?
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase unzips DNA and synthesizes mRNA using the non-coding (template) strand.

questions.prompt: To start transcription, RNA polymerase binds to which region of DNA?
questions.explanation: The promoter is upstream of a gene and rich in A and T. Promoter sequences are not transcribed.

why.B: The terminator signals the end of a gene.
why.C: The start codon begins translation on mRNA.
why.D: The operator is where an operon's repressor binds.

questions.prompt: Promoter regions are rich in which bases?
questions.explanation: Promoter: upstream, A/T rich (e.g., TATATAAT). Terminator: downstream, C/G rich.

why.B: C and G are rich in terminator regions.

questions.prompt: Which DNA strand is used as the template during transcription?

options.text: Whichever strand is closest to the ribosome

questions.explanation: RNA polymerase uses the non-coding (template) strand, so the mRNA matches the coding strand except U replaces T.

why.B: The coding strand matches the mRNA (with T instead of U).
why.C: Only one strand serves as the template.

questions.prompt: A DNA coding strand reads 5'-ATG TGT GAG-3'. What is the mRNA transcript?
questions.explanation: mRNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T.

why.B: That's complementary to the coding strand; mRNA matches the coding strand.
why.C: mRNA uses U instead of T.

questions.prompt: Using this codon wheel, which amino acid does the mRNA codon AUG code for?
questions.explanation: AUG is the start codon and codes for methionine (Met). It sets the reading frame.

why.A: AUU, AUC and AUA code for isoleucine; AUG is Met.

questions.prompt: Using this codon wheel, which amino acid does the codon UGG code for?
questions.explanation: Read the wheel from the center outward: U → G → G = Trp.

why.D: UGA is a stop codon; UGG is tryptophan.

questions.prompt: An mRNA codon is CAU. What is the tRNA anticodon?
questions.explanation: Anticodons are complementary to codons: C–G, A–U, U–A → GUA.

why.A: tRNA is RNA, so it uses U, not T.
why.C: The anticodon is complementary, not identical.
why.D: The anticodon is complementary to CAU.

questions.prompt: Stop codons such as UAA, UAG and UGA end translation because they:

options.text: Are rich in C and G

questions.explanation: No tRNAs exist for stop codons, so the ribosome lets go of the mRNA and releases the polypeptide.

why.B: RNA polymerase is used in transcription.

questions.prompt: What type of bond joins amino acids during translation?
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between amino acids in the ribosome (ATP is required).

why.B: Hydrogen bonds pair codons with anticodons.
why.D: Peptide bonds form the polypeptide backbone.

questions.prompt: Why can't you work out the exact codon from an amino acid?

options.text: Amino acids are made of DNA nucleotides
The code is redundant — most amino acids have several codons
tRNA anticodons are identical to the codons
Each codon codes for several amino acids

questions.explanation: Amino acids have multiple codons (except Met), so you can't determine the exact codon from the amino acid.

why.A: Amino acids are protein building blocks.
why.D: Each codon codes for one amino acid; the redundancy runs the other way.

questions.prompt: What is the Central Dogma of Biology?
questions.explanation: DNA is transcribed into mRNA, which is translated into protein.

why.B: Information flows from DNA to protein.
why.C: DNA is transcribed into RNA first.

questions.prompt: Where does transcription occur in bacteria?
questions.explanation: With no nucleus, bacterial transcription and translation both occur in the cytoplasm.

questions.prompt: Translation occurs at the ribosome. What is its product?
questions.explanation: The ribosome reads mRNA codons; tRNAs bring amino acids, which are joined by peptide bonds.

why.B: mRNA is the product of transcription.
